item.title: ‘The Further Mis-Adventures Of Cliff Booth’ Review: The Vibes Are Off In David Fincher’s Dark, Dank, Grubby Tarantino Episode
item.description: There’s a strong argument to be made that if you’ve read Quentin Tarantino ’s “ Once Upon A Time In Hollywood ” novelization, “ The Further Mis-Adventures Of Cliff Booth ” shouldn’t surprise you. Tarantino’s book was shaggy and baggy, like an unedited, freehand version of the movie, full of detours, tangents, and narrative cul-de-sacs. An interesting extended curiosity, mildly entertaining in spots, but much of it probably wouldn’t have stood on its own outside the pulp novel format. Continue reading ‘The Further Mis-Adventures Of Cliff Booth’ Review: The Vibes Are Off In David Fincher’s Dark, Dank, Grubby Tarantino Episode at The Playlist.

item.title: Christopher Nolan Says Fans Will Never See Deleted Scenes From 'The Odyssey': "I Want To Stand By The Film That Goes Out"
item.description: For those expecting deleted scenes on the home video release of Christopher Nolan 's " The Odyssey ,' here's some bad news. Variety reports that while there are "a lot of" them, they're not available on any of the new discs that hit stores this past Tuesday. And the scenes will never see the light of day either, because, as Nolan told The Independent in a new interview, "I don't really believe in director's cuts." READ MORE: Steven Spielberg Says 'The Odyssey' Is "One Of The Greatest Things" Matt Damon "Has Ever Done As An Actor," Also Praises Samantha Morton "There's a lot of deleted scenes scrumbled up in the wastebasket that no one will ever see," the director told the British outlet.
